nodes.rationale: Preserves the architecture doc's 8-phase contract and determinism guarantees; aligns 1:1 with the Stage 0-5 build model; cross-module data flow is typed frozen dataclasses so services cannot corrupt each other's state.

nodes.label: Networked microservices (rejected alternative)

nodes.label: Closed decision Q1: no plugin host, AI advisor, or MCP surface of any kind

nodes.label: Closed decision Q2: no hand-edit preservation on re-trim

nodes.label: Closed decision Q3: no concurrency/locking mechanism

nodes.norm_label: closed decision q3: no concurrency/locking mechanism

nodes.label: Closed decision Q6: UTF-8 read with Latin-1 fallback on decode failure (PW-02)

nodes.label: R1 -- Conflict Resolution and File Treatment (ordered overlay)
nodes.rationale: Base + selected features are folded left-to-right as an ordered overlay; the last layer that says something about a file/proc wins, so a feature can add, remove, or replace base content. Chosen so feature order is semantically authoritative for F1, F2, and F3 rather than an additive-only union of independent JSONs.
nodes.norm_label: r1 -- conflict resolution and file treatment (ordered overlay)

nodes.label: R2 -- Default Action Is Exclude
nodes.rationale: Default-exclude is fixed and non-configurable; a global default-include mode was rejected so trimming behavior stays predictable and no file survives without an explicit authoring decision.

nodes.label: R3 -- Tracing Is Default-On and Conservative
nodes.rationale: Tracing lowers authoring cost and trim risk during the 2-week delivery window by letting owners describe entry-point procs instead of enumerating full call chains. It is reporting-only by design: Chopper never guesses an unexpected proc into the surviving set, keeping users in full control via explicit JSON entries.
nodes.norm_label: r3 -- tracing is default-on and conservative

nodes.label: R4 -- F3 Uses Plain Strings by Design
nodes.rationale: Real flow steps are heterogeneous (filenames, source commands, ivar refs, #if/#else directives); forcing them into one rigid step datatype would recreate FlowBuilder-style complexity. Chopper trades full semantic validation for authoring flexibility, mitigated by cross-validation warnings against F1/F2 output.
nodes.norm_label: r4 -- f3 uses plain strings by design

nodes.label: R5 -- Backup-and-Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Chopper never edits a domain in place; it renames the original to `_backup` on first trim and always rebuilds from that clean backup on re-trim. Chosen for safety and clean re-trim over destructive incremental editing.
